reviews.pros:
I joined Zepto in July 2024 as a Quality Team Lead. Initially, we were provided with only 10 days of training, which felt insufficient for the responsibilities that followed. Despite being designated as a Quality Analyst Team lead, we were quickly asked to handle a high volume of live chats — 520 in total — which seemed more aligned with customer support responsibilities than quality analysis.
There appeared to be a lack of structured management and communication. Often, we were asked to switch between working from home and reporting to the office at very short notice, sometimes even on the same day. This unpredictability and lack of clear guidelines made it difficult to plan work effectively and maintain consistency in performance.
Additionally, the role expectations were blurred. Even while performing Quality Analyst duties, we were intermittently pulled into chat handling without clear boundaries or scheduling, further adding to the confusion and stress.
Overall, the lack of organization, undefined role clarity, and inconsistent communication significantly impacted the work environment and morale.
reviews.cons:
Over time, I found very little to appreciate about working at Zepto. The role demanded a six-day work week, but even the off days weren’t consistent or fairly managed. For instance, if an off day fell on a Monday, it was often shifted or denied altogether. As a result, the next off would only come the following Friday or Saturday, leading to long, uninterrupted stretches of work.
Work hours were frequently extended beyond the expected shift, with little regard for employee well-being. At this stage in my career, such prolonged and unstructured work hours were both physically and mentally taxing.
The situation was further compounded during the probation period. Management, despite being aware that many of us were new and still learning the ropes, issued notices without ensuring clarity or adequate support. It was evident that even the management team lacked a proper understanding of the processes and systems in place.
Toward the end of my tenure, on my last working day, they unexpectedly asked me to extend my stay. When I requested written confirmation of this change, they refused — and instead proceeded to release me on the very same day I had already indicated as my intended departure date. This last-minute handling reflected a continued pattern of poor communication and disorganization.
